days.topic: Chapter 12: Stress, Health, and Coping · Stress: What It Is, Where It Comes From
days.clue: Any event or situation that threatens or taxes us and sets off the body's alarm and coping reactions
days.card: Stress-OR sounds like an actor: it is the thing doing the pushing. The stress is your reaction; the stressor is the cause. Money and work top the Stress in America survey.

days.topic: Lesson 5: Flower, Fruits and Seeds · Androecium, Gynoecium, Flower Types
days.clue: Type of unisexual flower that is male: androecium present, gynoecium absent
days.card: Staminate = stamens only (male). Don't mix it up with pistillate, the female flower with only the gynoecium. Bisexual flowers have both.

days.topic: Chapter 12: Stress, Health, and Coping · Psychological Moderators of Stress
days.clue: Pretending a stressor does not exist; it is NOT one of the helpful moderators of stress
days.card: Hardiness, humor, control and support moderate stress. Ignoring the problem does not: the exam question is 'all EXCEPT pretending that stressors do not exist'.

days.topic: Lesson 5: Flower, Fruits and Seeds · Seeds
days.clue: Protective outer covering of a seed, also called the seed coat
days.card: Testa = seed coat; pericarp = fruit wall. A seed has three basic parts: embryo, endosperm (stored food) and the testa. In dicots, food sits in the cotyledons.

days.topic: Chapter 11: Personality: Theory and Measurement · Learning-Theory Perspectives
days.clue: Psychologist who developed social cognitive theory and ran the Bobo doll study
days.card: Bandura = observation: kids copy a model's aggression toward the Bobo doll. Social cognitive theory keeps behavior but adds person variables like self-efficacy.

days.clue: Bryophyte with a flat, leafy gametophyte anchored by rhizoids; the other bryophytes are mosses and hornworts
days.card: Bryophytes have no vascular tissue: mosses, hornworts, liverworts. The liverwort's body is flat and leafy, and rhizoids hold it down. Its sporophyte looks like a tiny palm tree.

days.topic: Chapter 11: Personality: Theory and Measurement · The Psychodynamic Perspective
days.clue: Unpleasant tension Freud said the ego fights with defense mechanisms such as repression
days.card: Repression is the ego's automatic ejection of anxiety-evoking ideas from awareness. Remember: defense mechanisms exist to cope with anxiety. Good luck on the eval!

days.clue: Salicylate that blocks COX irreversibly; low doses protect the heart by stopping platelet thromboxane A2
days.card: The only NSAID whose COX block is permanent, so the antiplatelet effect lasts the platelet's 7-10 day life. Loaded in MI after checking for bleeding.

days.topic: Lesson 7: Anti-Inflammatory Drugs · Inflammation, Prostanoids, Pain and Fever
days.clue: IL-1, IL-6 and TNF-alpha that reach the hypothalamus and raise the body's temperature set point
days.card: They make the hypothalamus release PGE2, so the body feels cold and shivers. Elderly and immunocompromised patients may not mount a fever at all.

days.topic: Lesson 7: Anti-Inflammatory Drugs · NSAIDs: Mechanism and Uses
days.clue: Propionic-acid NSAID that is first-line for primary dysmenorrhea, started before the flow begins
days.card: Sold as Advil and Medicol, so never take both. The usual dose is 400 mg every 4-6 hours; OTC only at 200 mg or less.

days.topic: Lesson 7: Anti-Inflammatory Drugs · NSAID Adverse Effects
days.clue: GI lesion NSAIDs cause by removing COX-1's protective prostaglandins; it can bleed or perforate
days.card: Ask about GI bleeding before any NSAID. COX-1 prostaglandins protect the stomach lining, so blocking both COX enzymes leaves it exposed.

days.clue: COX-2 selective agent chosen when the stomach needs sparing, but never after a heart attack or stroke
days.card: Kind to the stomach, careful with the heart: it spares COX-1, so TXA2 stays unopposed. Not a stronger painkiller than other NSAIDs.
